annotations.title: chainpeek: check a transfer recipient for address poisoning on Base, Ethereum or Robinhood Chain

description: chainpeek: Check a transfer recipient for address poisoning: lookalikes in the sender's history. For balance, gas and blacklist checks too use transfer_preflight; for OFAC use check_sanctions. Returns a `risk` (high | medium | low) for paying `to`: reads `from`'s transfers of one token (default USDC) over the last 24 hours by default (about 27 minutes on Base) and finds addresses with `to`'s first 4 and last 4 hex characters; each reason carries its evidence (tx hash, block, amount, direction). High: `to` was never paid and imitates an address `from` paid or a contact, or appears only in zero-value or dust transfers. Medium: a lookalike exists but `to` was paid or is a contact. Older history, other tokens and other lookalikes are not seen. Bad input is a 422, a failed read a 502 (neither charged). Typically 0.5-4 s. Price: USD 0.002. Free: 10 chain reads per IP per UTC day. Docs: https://tanod.dev/learn/address-poisoning-check-api.html

chain.description: ethereum, base or robinhood (Robinhood Chain, chain id 4663).

contacts.description: Addresses you trust; `to` is compared with them too, with no chain read.

dust_threshold.description: Incoming transfers below this many token units are dust: default 0.01 for USDC and USDT, else off; 0 turns it off.

from.description: The sending wallet whose transfer history is read.

lookback_blocks.description: Instead of `lookback_s`: the latest blocks to read; 0 checks `contacts` only.

lookback_s.description: Seconds of history to read (default 24 hours; public nodes serve only about 27 minutes on Base). Not with `lookback_blocks`.

to.description: The recipient about to be paid; must differ from `from`.

token.description: Only this token's transfers are read; on robinhood pass a contract address.

name: check_address_poisoning

error.description: Only on an error result: an object {code, message}, or the reason string of an x402 PaymentRequired object.
